The study investigates the magnetic properties of (Ga,Mn)N thin films in proximity to Mg-doped GaN.
The experimental approach used is improved-sensitivity integral SQUID magnetometry.
The structure of the investigated trilayer heterostructures is GaN:Mg / (Ga,Mn)N / GaN:Mg.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is between 3.8 and 4.8 nm.
The maximum concentration of Mn in the (Ga,Mn)N layer is 5%.
The neighboring GaN:Mg layers do not affect the spin-spin interactions in the central (Ga,Mn)N layer.
The study concludes that a more intensive technological effort is needed to break the deadlock in the effectiveness of simultaneous Mn- and Mg-codoping in GaN.
The method used to determine the Mn concentration in the (Ga,Mn)N layer is secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS).
The maximum concentration of Mn accumulation by diffusion process at the interface region is 0.0025%.
The mechanism of Mn diffusion through GaN is interstitial-substitutional mechanism through Ga vacancies.
The growth temperature of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is around 730°C.
The Ga flux used for the (Ga,Mn)N layer is 8.5×10−7 Torr BEP.
The Mn flux used for the (Ga,Mn)N layer is 1×10−6 Torr BEP.
The Mg content in the GaN:Mg cladding layers is varied from 0 to 2×10−8 Torr BEP.
The Mg concentration in the GaN:Mg cladding layers is between 3×10^17 cm−3 and 9×10^20 cm−3.
The Curie temperature of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is around 10 K.
